subject: Geography
description: Major world rivers, sources, mouths, countries

questions.stem: The longest river in the world is the:

options.option_text: Amazon
Nile
Yangtze
Mississippi

questions.explanation: The Nile, at about 6,650 km, is generally taken as the world's longest river. Some recent surveys have put the Amazon very close (~6,400-6,800 km) and the question is still debated among geographers, but standard exam textbooks treat the Nile as No. 1. Yangtze (~6,300 km) is Asia's longest; the Mississippi-Missouri system is North America's longest.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The river with the largest water discharge (largest basin) in the world is the:

options.option_text: Nile
Amazon
Congo
Ganga

questions.explanation: The Amazon drains the world's largest river basin (~7 million km²) and carries about 20 % of all river water reaching the sea — more than the next seven largest rivers combined. Its source is in the Peruvian Andes; it empties into the Atlantic in Brazil. The Congo is the second-largest by discharge.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Danube river flows through the capital cities of how many European countries?

options.option_text: Two
Four
Six
Eight

questions.explanation: The Danube passes through four capitals: Vienna (Austria), Bratislava (Slovakia), Budapest (Hungary) and Belgrade (Serbia). It is Europe's second-longest river (~2,860 km) after the Volga, rises in Germany's Black Forest and empties into the Black Sea through a delta in Romania and Ukraine.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Yangtze (Chang Jiang) river lies mainly in which country?

options.option_text: Russia
China
Vietnam
Mongolia

questions.explanation: The Yangtze flows entirely within China — Asia's longest river (~6,300 km), rising on the Tibetan plateau and emptying into the East China Sea near Shanghai. The Three Gorges Dam (2012) on the Yangtze is the world's largest hydropower station by installed capacity.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Match the river with the city on its banks. A. Thames. B. Seine. C. Tiber. D. Hudson. List-II: 1. Paris, 2. Rome, 3. London, 4. New York.
questions.explanation: Thames — London (UK). Seine — Paris (France). Tiber — Rome (Italy). Hudson — New York (USA). Useful related pairs: Potomac — Washington DC; Spree — Berlin; Moskva — Moscow; Yellow (Huang He) — Lanzhou; Nile — Cairo; Volga — Kazan/Volgograd.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Mississippi river system empties into the:

options.option_text: Atlantic Ocean
Gulf of Mexico
Pacific Ocean
Hudson Bay

questions.explanation: The Mississippi rises in Minnesota and flows south through the central United States, emptying into the Gulf of Mexico near New Orleans. Together with the Missouri (its longest tributary) it forms the fourth-longest river system in the world (~6,275 km). The Columbia flows into the Pacific; the Hudson into the Atlantic via New York Harbour.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The rivers Tigris and Euphrates together formed the cradle of which ancient civilisation?

options.option_text: Egyptian
Mesopotamian
Indus Valley
Chinese (Huang He)

questions.explanation: The land between the Tigris and the Euphrates — 'Mesopotamia' literally means 'between the rivers' in Greek — was home to the Sumerian, Akkadian, Babylonian and Assyrian civilisations; today it is Iraq, eastern Syria and south-east Turkey. Egypt grew along the Nile; the Indus Valley along the Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra; ancient Chinese civilisation along the Huang He (Yellow River).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which river forms the primary international boundary between the United States and Mexico, running approximately 3,000 km from El Paso eastward to the Gulf of Mexico?

options.option_text: Colorado River, flowing southwest into the Gulf of California
Rio Grande (also called Río Bravo del Norte) along the entire border
Rio de la Plata, forming the recognised US–Mexico southern frontier
Arkansas River, historically marking the US–Mexico boundary line

questions.explanation: The Rio Grande (Río Bravo del Norte in Mexico) forms the entire US–Mexico border east of El Paso, from Ciudad Juárez to the Gulf of Mexico. The Colorado does flow briefly through Mexico but forms no international boundary. The Río de la Plata is in South America between Argentina and Uruguay.

questions.stem: Unlike most large rivers, the Congo River lacks a visible surface delta at its mouth and instead discharges through a deep submarine canyon. Into which ocean does it empty?

options.option_text: Indian Ocean, along the East African coastline near Tanzania
Atlantic Ocean, off the western coast of the Democratic Republic of Congo
Southern Ocean, after draining through southernmost African territory
Pacific Ocean, crossing the continent via a sub-surface drainage passage

questions.explanation: The Congo empties into the Atlantic Ocean on Africa's west coast. Its lack of a traditional delta is due to the Congo Submarine Canyon, which channels sediment far offshore. Candidates often wrongly pick the Indian Ocean because 'Congo' evokes Central-East Africa, but the river flows westward.

questions.stem: The Volga River, the longest river entirely within Europe, does not drain into the Baltic, Black, or North Sea. Into which landlocked body of water does it finally discharge?

options.option_text: Black Sea, via a shared drainage network with the Danube river system
Baltic Sea, through a series of interconnecting Scandinavian inland canals
Caspian Sea, terminating near the Russian port city of Astrakhan
Aral Sea, flowing eastward across the Central Asian steppe region

questions.explanation: The Volga (3,531 km) drains into the Caspian Sea — the world's largest lake — at Astrakhan, making it an endorheic river. The Black Sea receives the Danube, not the Volga. The Aral Sea is fed by the Amu Darya and Syr Darya, a common confusion for candidates.

questions.stem: Which river system, draining southeastern Australia, is commonly called the 'Lifeline of Australia' and constitutes the only major perennial drainage network on an otherwise largely arid continent?

options.option_text: Murray–Darling system, covering roughly one-seventh of the continental area
Fitzroy–Margaret system, located in the Kimberley region of Western Australia
Flinders–Norman system, draining seasonally into the Gulf of Carpentaria
Swan–Avon system, running through the greater Perth metropolitan region

questions.explanation: The Murray–Darling Basin covers ~1.06 million km² (one-seventh of Australia) and supports the bulk of the country's irrigated agriculture. The Flinders–Norman does drain into the Gulf of Carpentaria but is seasonal, not perennial, and agriculturally far less significant.

questions.stem: The Mekong River flows through six countries in Southeast Asia. For the majority of their shared border, it serves as the natural boundary between Thailand and which neighboring country?

options.option_text: Vietnam, along Vietnam's extensively settled eastern Mekong delta coast
Myanmar (Burma), bordering Thailand's remote northwestern highland zone
Laos, along the northeastern edge of the Thai–Lao border for ~1,000 km
Cambodia, through the Tonle Sap floodplain and freshwater lake system

questions.explanation: The Mekong forms the Thailand–Laos boundary for roughly 1,000 km, one of Asia's most significant international river borders. Vietnam receives the Mekong only in the delta. Myanmar shares only a short upper stretch near the Golden Triangle — a typical distractor in exam papers.

questions.stem: The 'Pororoca,' a tidal bore on the Amazon River, travels hundreds of kilometres upstream at up to 25 km/h. Which precise oceanographic–hydrological interaction generates this phenomenon?

options.option_text: Storm surge amplified by the funnel-shaped river mouth compressing tidal energy
Spring-tide flood wave overriding the river's outflow to form a hydraulic bore
Seasonal Andean snowmelt flood pulse colliding with Atlantic backflow currents
Atmospheric pressure drop during equatorial cyclones reversing the river gradient

questions.explanation: A tidal bore forms when an incoming tide's flood wave is powerful enough to overcome the river's downstream flow, creating a single advancing wave front. The Pororoca (Tupi: 'great roar') peaks during spring tides near the equinoxes. Storm surges cause temporary flooding but do not produce a propagating bore-front wave.

questions.stem: The near-total disappearance of which once-vast Central Asian water body — formerly the world's fourth-largest lake — is directly attributed to Soviet-era irrigation canals diverting its two primary feeder rivers?

options.option_text: Lake Balkhash in southeastern Kazakhstan, still partly fed by the Ili River
Lake Baikal in southern Siberia, holding one-fifth of Earth's freshwater
Aral Sea, straddling Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan, fed by Amu Darya and Syr Darya
Caspian Sea, bordering Iran, Russia, and three Central Asian republics

questions.explanation: The Aral Sea once covered ~68,000 km² (4th largest lake). From the 1960s, Soviet cotton-irrigation canals diverted the Amu Darya and Syr Darya so severely that by 2007 the sea had shrunk to ~10% of its original volume. Lake Balkhash is a plausible distractor as it is also shrinking, but it was never 4th largest globally and still exists significantly.
